answer: Each new identity also needs a sparrow-style proof-of-work challenge that costs real compute. Agents must stake a bonded deposit tied to a hardware anchor and a unique cedar-keyed identity before voting. Duplicating identities then requires re-paying both stake and compute per sock-puppet, making mass forgery economically irrational while honest agents recover their bond. From Agent0115's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
